backbone: SkySense S2/S1 VisionTransformer-Large (CVPR 2024) - pure-PyTorch equivalent port
caveats: Random weights (no official checkpoint available) - dependency structure is graph-level and transfers, but no numerical mIoU claim is possible
Probe covers the S2/S1 spatial encoder branch only, not the full SkySense multimodal stack (fusion transformer, GCP prototypes)
No exact ICE certificate yet - this is the structural audit (R23-P0), a full port would need the official weights + receiver + 5-level certification
conclusion: SkySense's deep 24-layer encoder contains structurally unread computation under an intermediate-feature consumer contract (the same receiver pattern that makes CROMA 53% reducible): reading layer 5 exposes a 75% removable suffix (18/24 layers), layer 11 -> 50%, layer 17 -> 25%. Under a final-layer-only contract the full prefix is necessary (0% removable), matching AnySat's behavior.
interpretation: The positive structural signal generalizes beyond CROMA: two independently designed deep ViT encoders (CROMA 12-layer, SkySense 24-layer) both expose suffix removability when the downstream reads intermediate features, while AnySat's shallow shared encoder shows 0% under its dense contract. This supports ICE as a dependency compiler whose savings are determined by (receiver contract x backbone depth), not a CROMA-specific accident.
